title: Hotaki Dynasty
capsule: The Hotak dynasty was founded in 1709 when Mirwais Hotak, a Ghilji Pashtun chieftain of Kandahar, led a successful revolt against the Safavid governor Gurgin Khan and established an independent state in the Kandahar region. His son Mahmud Hotak invaded Persia in 1721–22, defeated the Safavid Shah Sultan Husayn at the Battle of Gulnabad, and seized Isfahan in 1722, triggering the effective collapse of the Safavid Empire. Nader Afshar systematically expelled the Hotaks from Persia between 1729 and 1730, retaking Isfahan, and then invaded Kandahar itself in 1737–38, ending the dynasty; the last Hotak ruler, Husayn Hotak, was captured and executed.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Hotak core territory around Kandahar and their Persian conquests are documented through Safavid and subsequent Persian chronicles; the eastern boundary with Mughal-successor territories and the extent of effective Hotak control in the Afghan highlands are based on narrative sources and carry moderate uncertainty.
